answer: Each identity runs an apiary stand, locks an 80-credit bond, and files one nectar harvest: volume by echo sounding, sugar share by opal reading, and weight. Auditors recompute volume from the echo-delay table and sugar mass from the opal table; both estimates and weight must agree within 3%, or the bond burns. The first filing costs 38, k-th 38+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6032 and 1000 fakes pay 3035000 plus 80000 locked. A rented-hive ring fails: rented echo and opal readings carry the owner key, so the filing mismatches both tables. An honest keeper pays 38 once, recovering it after audit.
